reasoning:
**What is asked.** Donald Trump's net approval on 31 December 2026 in the Silver Bulletin average, in percentage points.

**Starting point.** The Silver Bulletin average hit an all-time low of -24.3 on 23 October 2026 after -23.9 the week before. It then recovered slightly: approval was 38.4% on 2 November and 37.6% on 12 November (Silver Bulletin; Newsweek, November 2026), which puts the net figure in the low minus-twenties, roughly -22 to -24.

**Recent evidence.** Individual polls taken after the 3 November midterms are worse than the average: The Economist/YouGov had him at -31 (9 to 11 November), a record low for that series, and another tracker moved from -19 to -26. Averages lag single polls, so some further decline is likely to feed through. Against that, his rating has repeatedly bounced a point or two after each new low this year.

**How much it can move.** Over six-week stretches in 2026 the average has typically moved by two to three points, and by about five in its largest swings (for example -7.5 to -13.0 during the autumn 2025 shutdown). I centre on -23.5 with a standard deviation of roughly 2.7 points, skewed slightly toward further decline.

**What would move it outside my range.** A quick end to the Iran war or a strong rally-round event could lift it above -19; a new shock on prices or a damaging personnel fight could push it below -29.

**Forecast.** Median -23.5, with 90% of the probability between -28.5 and -19.5.
question_title: What will be Donald Trump's net approval on December 31, 2026?
